label: Scraping & browser
insluit_regel: Hosted, commercially callable scraping or browser-automation APIs with broad adoption, one row per flagship offering from a distinct provider.

assen.label: the strongest anti-bot unblocking
assen.caveat: Unblocking strength is an ordinal Syftly coding (high=3/medium=2/low=1) from the sources, not a measured number.

assen.label: the highest success rate
assen.caveat: Success rates are the weakest figures here: target-dependent, never first-hand, and contradictory between benchmarks.

providers.sterk: Highest independently-measured success rate (98.44% in Scrape.do's benchmark of 11 providers) on heavily protected sites, with pay-per-success billing and the largest proxy network.
providers.zwak: Returns raw HTML, not LLM-ready markdown/JSON; the effective per-request price varies by plan and target (ScrapeCreators cites $0.75-$2.50/1000) and the success rate comes from a benchmark published by a competitor (Scrape.do).
providers.bron: Tier 1: brightdata.com/pricing/web-unlocker ($1.50/1000 PAYG; Scale $499/mo for 383k requests = $1.30/1000; 5000 free requests/month). Tier 2: Scrape.do benchmark via scrapecreators.com (98.44%).

providers.sterk: Top score (93.14%) in Proxyway's independent 2025 benchmark across 15 heavily protected sites; pays only for successful responses and offers AI-driven automatic extraction to structured data.
providers.zwak: Price is strongly tier-dependent: HTTP $0.13-$1.27/1000, browser rendering $1.01-$16.08/1000, plus separate extraction fees — so it is not directly comparable (the value is a light estimate for an average target). As of August 2026 Zyte no longer publishes tier pricing publicly (login-gated cost estimator), so these June 2026 figures can no longer be re-verified from the page.
providers.bron: Tier 1: docs.zyte.com/zyte-api/pricing (HTTP $0.13-$1.27/1000, browser $1.01-$16.08/1000). Tier 2: Proxyway 2025 benchmark (93.14%).

providers.sterk: Strongest LLM-ready output (direct markdown/JSON with schema extraction), cheap per page ($0.00083/page on Standard) and 69% success in Scrapeway's August 2026 test — better than ScrapingBee (48%) in that same test.
providers.zwak: Lower reliability on heavily protected sites than the unblocking specialists; Stealth Mode and /extract can cost up to ~5 credits per request, sharply raising the effective price (the pricing page lists only the 1 credit/page base rate, so the stealth multiplier is not vendor-confirmed).
providers.bron: Tier 1: firecrawl.dev/pricing (Standard $83/mo billed yearly = 100k credits -> $0.83/1000 pages; scrape/crawl/map 1 credit per page). Tier 2: scrapeway.com benchmark run 8-14 Aug 2026 (69%, 4.1s).

providers.sterk: Cheapest base rate in the field ($0.099/1000 base requests on Startup) and offers AI extraction; simple API with good docs.
providers.zwak: JS rendering is on by default and costs 5 credits (premium proxy 10, premium+JS 25, stealth proxy 75), so real cost is far higher — hence not comparable; success rate is heavily disputed between benchmarks (84.47% at Proxyway 2025 vs 48% at Scrapeway August 2026), so left null.
providers.bron: Tier 1: scrapingbee.com/pricing (Startup $99.99/mo = 1M credits -> $0.099/1000 base) and help.scrapingbee.com credit-system article (JS 5, premium 10, premium+JS 25, stealth 75 credits). Tier 2: Proxyway 2025 (84.47%) and Scrapeway August 2026 (48%) — mutually contradictory.

providers.sterk: Low base rate (~$0.149/1000 credits on Startup) with a simple proxy+rendering API and a generous free tier (1000 credits/month).
providers.zwak: Lowest independent success rate of the tested set on protected sites (68.95% at Proxyway 2025); credits add up fast (JS 5-10x, anti-bot +10, Google 25, LinkedIn 30) so price is not comparable; barely any LLM-ready output.
providers.bron: Tier 1: scraperapi.com/pricing (Startup $149/1M credits -> $0.149/1000 base). Tier 2: Proxyway 2025 benchmark (68.95%).

providers.sterk: Broadest platform: 61,000+ ready-made Actors, full browser automation (Playwright/Puppeteer) and LLM-ready crawlers (Website Content Crawler -> markdown); free tier with $5 credits/month.
providers.zwak: Price is Compute-Unit-/Actor-dependent and therefore unpredictable (~$0.20/1000 via HTTP up to $0.50-$5.00/1000 with a browser, plus separate proxy and data-transfer fees) — not comparable as a fixed per-request price; no independent aggregate success rate, as results vary per Actor.
providers.bron: Tier 1: apify.com/pricing (Starter $29/mo incl. $29 credits, $0.20/CU; 1 CU = 1 GB-hour) and apify.com/apify/website-content-crawler ($0.20/1000 pages raw HTTP, $0.50-$5/1000 headless browser). No independent platform-level success benchmark.

providers.sterk: Pure cloud-browser infrastructure built for AI agents: full programmable browser automation (Playwright/Puppeteer/CDP), per-hour billing and 25 concurrent browsers from $20/month (100 concurrent on the $99 Startup plan).
providers.zwak: No ready-made unblocking/anti-bot layer or LLM-ready extraction (raw browser output); billing per browser-hour ($0.10-$0.12/hour) + proxy per GB does not convert to per-request — the $0.05/1000 is a rough light estimate and therefore not comparable; no independent success benchmark.
providers.bron: Tier 1: docs.browserbase.com/guides/plans-and-pricing (Developer $20/mo, 100 browser-hours, 25 concurrent, $0.12/hour overage; 1 GB proxy included then $12/GB. Startup $99/mo, 500 hours, 100 concurrent, $0.10/hour). Per-request price is a derived light estimate.

best-web-scraping-api-for-article-extrac.query: Best web scraping API for article extraction
best-web-scraping-api-for-article-extrac.hap: For pulling clean article text from news sites and blogs, Firecrawl is the strongest default: direct markdown and JSON output with schema extraction, priced at $0.83 per 1000 requests on its Standard plan. When articles sit behind heavy anti-bot protection, Bright Data's Web Unlocker at $1.50 per 1000 requests had the highest independently-reported success rate; Zyte API adds AI-driven automatic extraction to structured data. A light estimate from public benchmarks and pricing, August 2026.

best-web-scraping-api.hap: Web scraping splits by job. For blocked, anti-bot-heavy sites, Bright Data's Web Unlocker had the highest independently-reported success rate and the strongest unblocking, and is the safe default. Firecrawl is the cheapest comparable per-request rate and purpose-built for LLM-ready content; Zyte adds full browser automation with clean structured output. Pricing models differ wildly and success rates conflict between benchmarks, so this is a light estimate, August 2026.

cheapest-web-scraping-api.hap: Among providers with a clean, comparable per-request price, Firecrawl is the cheapest at about $0.83 per 1000 pages, ahead of Bright Data's Web Unlocker (around $1.50). The lower headline rates from ScrapingBee, ScraperAPI, Apify and Browserbase are credit- or compute-priced with multipliers (JS rendering alone can cost 5x), so they are not directly comparable and are excluded. A light estimate from provider pricing pages, August 2026.

best-web-scraping-api-for-blocked-sites.query: Best web scraping API for blocked and anti-bot sites
best-web-scraping-api-for-blocked-sites.hap: For heavily protected, anti-bot sites, Bright Data's Web Unlocker leads on both unblocking strength and the highest independently-reported success rate (98.44%), ahead of Zyte (93.14%). Treat success rates as the weakest figures here: they are target-dependent, conflict sharply between benchmarks (ScrapingBee's reported rate differs widely across two separate tests), and Bright Data's number comes from a competitor-published benchmark. A light estimate, not a first-hand measurement.

web-scraping-api-with-llm-ready-output.query: Web scraping API with LLM-ready output
web-scraping-api-with-llm-ready-output.hap: For output you can hand straight to an LLM, Zyte is the highest-ranked option that returns clean structured data with AI-driven extraction, and Firecrawl is purpose-built for it with direct markdown and JSON plus schema extraction. ScrapingBee and Apify also offer AI extraction, while Bright Data and ScraperAPI return raw HTML. A light estimate from provider documentation, June 2026.
